node.title: Dyadic primitive first-owner antipodal subtraction
node.statement: For a cyclic evaluation subgroup of order n=2^s in odd characteristic, let T(n,t,b) count b-subsets with their first t power sums zero and let T_prim restrict to trivial rotation stabilizer. Then T_prim(n,t,b)=T(n,t,b) for odd b and T_prim(n,t,b)=T(n,t,b)-T(n/2,floor(t/2),b/2) for even b. Thus interval-restricted primitive counts require one exact subtraction. For even t, X_prim(n,t)=X(n,t)-(q^(t/2)/2^(n/2))X(n/2,t/2).
node.attack_surface: Check the cyclic 2-group stabilizer criterion, the odd/even moment descent, every fixed-weight boundary, and the normalization factor.
node.falsifier: A nonprimitive subset not invariant under the order-two shift, a paired lift whose descended moments disagree, or a fixed-weight/normalized count violating the formula.
node.notes: This pays the first-owner deletion interface only. It gives no upper bound on the remaining primitive term.
